item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 300553
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, on
upgraded Hurricane Rachel, located a couple hundred miles
south-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, and on Tropical
Depression Nineteen-E, located over the western East Pacific.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this weekend or early next
week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development
while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Roberts

----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the remnants of Polo were located near

item.description:
Issued at 500 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 301134
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Intermediate Advisory Number 13A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
500 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES MOVING NORTHWESTWARD...
...COULD BECOME A MAJOR HURRICANE IN A DAY OR SO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM MST...1200 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.8N 107.6W
ABOUT 355 MI...570 KM W OF LAZARO CARDENAS MEXICO
ABOUT 220 MI...350 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico north of Playa Perula to Cabo
Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM MST (1200 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 17.8 North, longitude 107.6 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A northwestward motion 
at a slower forward speed is expected during the next day or two, 
followed by a turn toward the west-northwest and west later this 
week. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to 
move away from mainland Mexico and south of the Baja California 
Peninsula through Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Rapid strengthening is expected today, and Rachel could 
become a major hurricane within the next day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160
miles (260 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions will continue in portions of the
warning area this morning. Tropical storm conditions are possible
in the watch area this morning.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches, with isolated maximum totals of 12 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, Michoacán, Colima and
Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the southwestern coast 
of Mexico during the next couple of days and spread northward along 
the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula 
through the end of the week. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
833 
WTPZ43 KNHC 300849
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026

Rachel is becoming better organized as the north-northeasterly 
vertical wind shear over the system appears to be relaxing.  After 
strengthening into a hurricane around 0600 UTC, the system is 
developing better-defined convective banding features, 
especially over the western quadrant of the circulation.  Deep 
convection remains very intense, with numerous cloud tops as cold 
as -80 deg C.  A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft flying a research 
mission into Rachel measured 84-kt winds at the 700 mb flight 
level.  Based on this observation and the increased organization on 
satellite images, the advisory intensity is set to 75 kt.  This is 
somewhat higher than the subjective Dvorak estimate and objective 
estimates from UW-CIMSS.

The forward speed has slowed somewhat and the current motion 
estimate is 315/9 kt.  Rachel continues to move along the 
southwestern side of a mid-tropospheric ridge over northern and 
central Mexico.  The ridge is weakening due to the passage of a 
mid- to upper-level trough/low over the southern United States, and 
this is gradually slowing the steering current.  As the low lifts 
northward during the next couple of days, this should allow another 
ridge to build to the north of the tropical cyclone.  As a result, 
Rachel is forecast to turn toward the west-northwest and pass well 
south of the Baja California Peninsula before continuing westward 
away from land. The official track forecast is similar to, but 
slightly slower than, the previous NHC prediction.  This is a blend 
of the latest HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google 
DeepMind guidance.

Given the decrease in vertical shear, and expected passage over 
very warm waters, significant strengthening seems likely during the 
next 24-36 hours.  The SHIPS Rapid Intensification (RI) guidance 
indicates a substantially higher than normal probability of RI.  
The official intensity forecast anticipates that Rachel will 
quickly strengthen into a major hurricane by tomorrow if not 
sooner.  This is also similar to the latest HCCA prediction.
Beyond 48 hours, drier low- to mid-level air could cause some 
weakening.  The NHC intensity forecasts is on the high side of the 
model guidance envelope.

The outer wind radii were adjusted based on data from recent 
ASCAT-B/C overpasses.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of
Mexico, tropical-storm-force winds are expected along a portion of
the coast of southwestern Mexico in the warning area this morning.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will bring locally heavy rainfall to 
portions of coastal southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the southwestern and west-central coast of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula during the next several
days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  30/0900Z 17.6N 107.2W   75 KT  85 MPH
 12H  30/1800Z 18.4N 108.1W   90 KT 105 MPH
 24H  01/0600Z 19.2N 109.1W  100 KT 115 MPH

$$

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 300837
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 AM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026

Apart from some intermittent bursts of deep convection north and 
east of the center, Tropical Depression Nineteen-E is all but devoid 
of convection. Visible satellite imagery continues to depict a 
closed circulation, albeit slightly elongated. A 0531 UTC METOP-C 
scatterometer pass confirmed an elongated circulation, with peak 
winds of around 20 kt surrounding the center. The latest TAFB Dvorak 
fix was T2.0/30 kt. Based on a blend of these data, the initial 
intensity is held at 25 kt.
 
The initial motion has shifted slightly east-southeastward, now at 
110/08 kt. The depression is expected to maintain a generally 
east-southeastward path, with slight wobbles in its track, as it is 
steered by a northward-displaced monsoon trough. The updated NHC 
track forecast is largely unchanged from the previous advisory, 
roughly in between the simple (TVCN) and corrected consensus (HCCA) 
aids.

Nineteen-E is forecast to remain in a relatively hostile environment 
marked by moderate vertical wind shear within a moisture-starved 
environment. The depression is anticipated to degenerate into a 
post-tropical remnant low within 36 h, but given how little 
convection has persisted over the last several hours, it is very 
possible that this transition could occur sooner. The biggest source 
of uncertainty in the forecast is the degree to which diurnally 
enhanced convection will occur, if at all. The latest intensity 
forecast keeps the depression's strength steady through the forecast 
period, following the middle of the model envelope, with dissipation 
still expected to occur within 60 h.
